transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Gupta (Astral CTO), Ben Alvarez (Astral ML Eng), Sofia Mendes (Astral Data Eng)

Summary: Discovery focused on embeddings + reranking architecture. Customer (Astral Analytics) evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment, vector DB integration (weaviate/pinecone), embedding dimensionality, throughput targets, and hybrid search (BM25 + vector). Action items and next steps captured.

Topics: embeddings dimensionality, vector DB vs native Redwood embedding index, hybrid search, throughput/batching, dedicated capacity, VPC/private deployment, SOC2/compliance questions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm lena park from Redwood — i'll kick us off. Marcus from our SE team is here to go deeper on the architecture.
[00:15] Priya (Astral CTO): thanks lena, appreciate it. we want to understand tradeoffs — cost and latency mainly — and if we should run hosted or dedicated. ben and sofia are on to scope the POC.
[00:35] Marcus (Redwood SE): great; quick agenda — current stack, data size, qps targets, embedding dims, and any security/compliance must-haves. then i'll sketch a couple options and recommended POC plan. sound good?
[00:48] Ben (Astral ML Eng): yep sounds good. currently we run a microservice on AWS, metadata in postgres, search backed by elastic for keyword and pinecone for vectors — cost is creeping up and we have some latency spikes.
[01:05] Sofia (Astral Data Eng): also we have mixed document types — long docs, short transcripts — and want to support hybrid search: bm25 + vector reranking.
[01:20] Priya: timeline: pilot in 2 weeks, production in 2 months if pilot shows win. SLA target 95th pct latency under 200ms for top-k queries.
[01:35] Marcus: okay, quick clarifying Qs — what's your peak qps for search, and expected average vector dimensionality?
[01:45] Ben: peak qps around 120 qps, average ~35 qps. for dims we've been using 512 for now but open to suggestions.
[02:02] Lena: just to set expectations — hosted can get you started fastest, dedicated gives predictable throughput and better tail latency; private/VPC for strict data residency or SOC2 needs.
[02:18] Priya: we do need SOC2 and SSO, but not sure yet if on-prem is required. also curious about how Redwood integrates with our vector DBs. we currently use pinecone.
[02:33] Marcus: Redwood's hosted API returns embeddings and can also act as model/rerank layer; for vector storage you can continue using Pinecone or Weaviate. we also offer integrated indexing on dedicated clusters — so you can either push embeddings to your vector DB or route queries through Redwood for rerank.
[02:55] Ben: what's the implication on latency if we do external vector DB vs keeping rerank in Redwood?
[03:05] Marcus: good question — network hops add variance. pattern we recommend for low-latency: do nearest-neighbor search in your vector DB to get top-N candidates (e.g., 200), then call Redwood reranker for final scoring — that means one extra model call but reduces model compute because you score a small set. If you host reranker on dedicated capacity in the same region and use VPC peering, tail latency can be sub-200ms.
[03:32] Sofia: 200 candidates seems high — we usually do 50. how does candidate size affect cost?
[03:38] Marcus: candidate size is linear in reranker compute — scoring 200 vs 50 is roughly 4x compute. so cost and latency scale. for many workloads 50–100 is a sweet spot.
[03:54] Priya: embedding dims — we've seen docs recommending 768 or 512. what's Redwood's guidance?
[04:02] Marcus: depends on model and retrieval quality. smaller dims (256) are cheaper and faster for vector DB indexing, but may lose some nuance. we typically recommend starting with 512 for production-quality semantic search; during POC we can try 256/512/768 A/B to measure recall/latency tradeoffs.
[04:20] Ben: our storage costs on pinecone are a concern. do you have quantized embeddings or downstream compression?
[04:28] Lena: Redwood Optimize gives quantization recommendations and sometimes you can run 8-bit or PQ on the DB side. we also suggest dimensionality reduction experiments in the POC. we'll share concrete config options.
[04:42] Sofia: about throughput — if we hit 120 qps peak, what's the recommended deployment? hosted vs dedicated?
[04:51] Marcus: peak 120 qps with reranking — if you expect spikes and need consistent tail latency, dedicated reserved capacity is safer. hosted can handle bursts but your SLOs are best met with dedicated pools (autoscaling + burst). for initial pilot hosted is fine while we benchmark.
[05:08] Priya: what about hybrid search — combining bm25 for recall then vector rerank — any gotchas?
[05:14] Marcus: common approach: run bm25 on Elastic to get broad recall (top 500), run vector ANN on a vector DB for semantic matches (top 200), merge candidate sets then rerank. watch out for duplication and candidate normalization; we recommend a simple dedupe and metadata weighting during rerank.
[05:33] Ben: how do we route user queries? do we call Redwood for embeddings or compute locally?
[05:40] Lena: you can either call Redwood embeddings API then push vectors to your DB, or run model inference entirely on Dedicated/Private if you need local-only processing. Hosted embeddings is fastest to prototype.
[05:55] Priya: security — do you provide KMS integration and audit logs?
[06:00] Marcus: yes — KMS/HSM integrations available for Private; Dedicated supports customer-managed keys in some setups, plus audit logs and SSO/SAML. we'll send SOC2 docs and a security whitepaper.
[06:12] Sofia: any limitations on embedding size or throughput on hosted?
[06:16] Marcus: hosted has quotas but supports high throughput; we'll need to validate your exact qps pattern. Dedicated lets you reserve GPUs sized to throughput. we can run a benchmark to map qps to instance types.
[06:30] Priya: ok, POC shape — would you recommend we run two tracks: (1) hosted embeddings -> pinecone -> Redwood rerank; (2) dedicated cluster with integrated indexing?
[06:40] Marcus: exactly. Track 1 for speed of iteration; Track 2 to measure production economics and tail latency. we'll help with datasets and benchmarking harness.
[06:52] Ben: about cost, can we get an approximate cost per 1k queries for both tracks?
[06:58] Lena: we'll send a pricing spreadsheet with sample math. it's dependent on candidate size and model choice. we'll surface per-token + per-embedding costs and estimate inference compute for rerank.
[07:12] Priya: model choices — are you recommending a specific reranker model?
[07:16] Marcus: for reranking we usually use a cross-encoder style model; size depends on desired latency. We can start with a mid-size LLM (e.g., 7B family quantized) for balance of quality and latency, and test smaller/larger variants in the POC.
[07:30] Ben: do you have prebuilt connectors for pinecone and weaviate?
[07:34] Marcus: yes, we have integrations and example code. for pinecone we have sample ingestion scripts and for Weaviate same; we'll share repos.
[07:44] Sofia: what about dimensionality reduction during ingest — is that handled client-side?
[07:50] Marcus: typically you produce embeddings from the model and push them as-is. if you want to run PCA or product quantization, that's usually on your side or within the vector DB, but Redwood Optimize can recommend config and we can help with scripts.
[08:04] Priya: SLA and fallbacks — if dedicated cluster has an outage do you have automatic fallback to hosted?
[08:10] Lena: yes — routing policies allow fallback to hosted/model variants. we can set canary and A/B rollouts; for critical routes we recommend multi-tier policies.
[08:20] Ben: metrics we care about for the POC?
[08:23] Marcus: latency p50/p95/p99, cost per query, recall@k, MRR, and inference CPU/GPU utilization. also track token counts for per-token billing.
[08:36] Priya: sample dataset — we'll share 10k documents, with expected query mix skewed to short queries.
[08:43] Lena: perfect. Marcus — could you outline the benchmark steps now?
[08:48] Marcus: sure: 1) ingest 10k docs, produce embeddings at dims 256/512/768; 2) index to Pinecone and optionally Redwood integrated index; 3) run synthetic qps tests (steady-state at 35 qps and spike to 120 qps); 4) measure rerank latency for candidate sets of 50/100/200; 5) capture quality metrics (recall@10, mrr) across dims. we'll provide the harness.
[09:15] Ben: realistic spikes are sudden — can your dedicated autoscaler handle quick bursts?
[09:20] Marcus: autoscaling has limits — for hard SLOs we recommend reserved capacity + burst headroom. autoscale can fill gaps but ramp times vary by infra.
[09:30] Sofia: what's the expected time to integrate SSO and audit logs?
[09:34] Lena: SSO (SAML) and basic audit logs are typically configured during onboarding — a week or two depending on customer IT responsiveness.
[09:44] Priya: any regulatory or data residency constraints?
[09:47] Sofia: EU customer data must remain in eu-west-1 region. we need to confirm region availability.
[09:53] Marcus: we support regional deployments; Dedicated/Private can be provisioned in specific cloud regions. we'll verify eu-west-1 capacity.
[10:03] Ben: client-side vector compression — are there recommended libraries?
[10:06] Marcus: FAISS PQ is common; quantization in Pinecone via their options too. we'll include references in the repo.
[10:14] Priya: are there any example customers with similar scale you can share?
[10:18] Lena: yes — anonymized case study of a SaaS search team that moved from Pinecone+Elastic to Redwood Dedicated and cut cost by ~30% while improving p95 latency. we'll share the deck.
[10:30] Ben: what about retraining embeddings or model drift monitoring?
[10:34] Marcus: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets. we can set up nightly checks during POC.
[10:43] Sofia: for storage — if we reduce dims from 512 to 256, what's the rough reduction in storage?
[10:48] Marcus: roughly 50% reduction in vector storage size; actual depends on dtype and any PQ.
[10:55] Priya: any hard limits on candidate k or top-k?
[10:58] Marcus: no hard algorithmic limits but practical limits exist due to latency and cost. top-200 is common upper-bound for reranking.
[11:07] Ben: curious about model caching and kv cache — does it help rerank use case?
[11:11] Marcus: kv cache helps autoregressive generation; rerank (cross-encoder) is usually single-pass scoring so KV cache isn't as relevant. but if you do multi-stage generation + rerank, caches can help for repeated prefixes.
[11:25] Lena: ok let's recap next steps — we'll send pricing and security docs, Marcus will send benchmark harness and connectors, and Astral will share sample dataset and expected query mix.
[11:37] Priya: sounds good. can you target sending docs by Monday?
[11:40] Lena: yes — we'll target Monday (2027-06-07). Marcus anything to add?
[11:44] Marcus: just that we'll draft a two-track POC plan in a follow-up email with timelines.
[11:49] Ben: great, thanks everyone.
[11:52] Lena: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invite for POC kickoff.
[11:58] Priya: bye.

Notes on transcript quality: Some transcription artifacts present; proper nouns like 'Pinecone' occasionally transcribed or spelled similarly. Natural speech disfluencies retained.
